transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I came in because my head just feels foggy. I’m having trouble keeping my place in my cataloguing notes at work, even the old ones I know, and sometimes I can’t seem to decide what simple thing to do next. It’s been worrying me.
Does your foggy feeling tend to come and go over the course of the day?

I haven’t really noticed a clear pattern through the day. It’s more that when it hits, my mind just feels foggy, and I lose my place in cataloguing notes I should know, or I get stuck trying to decide the next simple thing to do.
Did this foggy thinking come on suddenly, or has it been building up gradually?
It’s been more gradual, I think. The low mood and the fogginess have been there most days for maybe about three months now—around when I started getting ready to leave the library.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days?

Yes. Most days lately I feel pretty down. I’ll sit at the kitchen table and it’s like the color’s gone out of everything. Even looking at my old watercolor books, which I used to enjoy, just makes me feel heavy instead of interested.
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people don’t seem to?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t been hearing voices or seeing things that aren’t there, at least not that I’ve noticed.
Have you started believing things that other people say aren’t true?
No... I don’t think so. I haven’t had anything like that, where people are telling me I’m believing something that isn’t real.
Have you been forgetting recent conversations or appointments?

Yes, I’ve been having trouble with that kind of thing. My mind feels foggy, and I lose track of what I’m doing. Even with my old cataloguing notes, I can’t keep my place, and sometimes I just sit there not able to decide what simple thing to do next.
Do you often repeat the same question or story because you’ve forgotten you already said it?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed myself repeating the same question or story a lot. If I do, no one’s really pointed it out to me.
Have you gotten lost in places that used to be familiar to you?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t gotten lost in places I know. I might feel a little unsure sometimes, but I usually know where I am.
Have you been having trouble managing your bills or finances?

Yes, I’ve been having trouble with that. It’s not just bills exactly, but paperwork in general piles up on me now. I used to be able to keep lecture plans, travel notes, household forms, things like that in order, and lately I just can’t seem to organize it reliably.
Have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yes. Most days lately I just sit at the kitchen table, and it feels like the color’s gone out of everything. I used to like looking through my old watercolor books, but now even those just make me feel heavy instead of interested.
Have you been waking up much earlier than usual and unable to get back to sleep?
Yes. I go to bed tired, but then I wake up around four in the morning and I can’t really get back to sleep. I just lie there thinking about what I’m supposed to do with myself now.
When someone encourages you or helps you get started, does your thinking usually become clearer?
Not really. Even if someone helps me start, my mind still feels foggy. I lose my place in my old cataloguing notes, and I have trouble deciding what simple thing to do next.
Have you been thinking that life isn’t worth living?
I… I don’t really know how to answer that. I’ve felt pretty low, but I’m not sure I’d say I’ve been thinking that exactly.
Have you been having thoughts of killing yourself?
I’m not sure. I don’t think I’ve been making any plans or anything like that. It’s more just… I feel very low and tired of things, but I don’t know if I’d call it wanting to kill myself.
Do you ever lose track of what day or date it is?
I don’t so much lose the day or date. It’s more that my mind feels foggy, and I can’t keep my place in my cataloguing notes or decide what simple thing to do next.
Have you been worrying a lot, more days than not?
I don’t know that I’d say I’m worrying a lot most days. I mean, I do get bothered by things, but I haven’t really been keeping track of it like that.
Have you become confused about where you are?
No, I don’t think so. I usually know where I am. I might feel a bit out of it sometimes, but not like I’m confused about my location.
Have you been having trouble finding the right words when you speak?

Sometimes, yes. It’s more like my mind gets foggy and I can’t keep my place in what I’m saying, kind of like with my cataloguing notes. I’ll pause because I’m trying to figure out the next simple word or thought.
Even on a day when your mood feels a little lighter, do the memory and thinking problems still stay about the same?

Yes, it pretty much stays the same. Even if I feel a little better mood-wise, my mind still feels foggy. I still lose my place in my cataloguing notes, or I’ll just sit there trying to decide what simple thing I’m supposed to do next.

final_diagnosis.reason: Progressive cognitive symptoms are prominent and persist independently of mood variation, including memory problems, executive dysfunction, disorganization with paperwork/finances, and word-finding difficulty, without psychosis or disorientation. This pattern is more consistent with mild cognitive disorder than primary major depression, schizophrenia, or generalized anxiety. Alzheimer disease remains an etiologic consideration, but the interview supports the syndrome diagnosis of mild cognitive disorder rather than established dementia.
